newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - retreating as durables leap.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - retreating as durables leap.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds fell at least 1/8 in early trade Wednesday, reacting to a surprising surge in orders for durable goods, which pressured a market already made wary by a monetary tightening.

The Federal Reserve on Tuesday fulfilled the market's expectations by raising the key federal funds rate by 25 basis points, but the 1.5 percent gain in orders for durable goods--items that last more than three years--immediately triggered fears the central bank might have to act again.
"People are wondering if that's enough," a trader said.
The February durable goods report, which showed fairly broad-based strength, had been expected to show orders fell 0.4 percent, according to a consensus poll of economists by Reuters.

The top deal, Hawaii's sale of $584 million of general obligation bonds was priced with a top yield of 5.75 percent in 2017, according to Smith Barney. Traders had expected the deal's rates to be raised around five basis points in the long end from the preliminary scale seen on Wednesday, before the central bank raised rates.

Noting that despite the state's recent downgrade by Standard & Poor's Corp., the credit still was high enough to be bought by insurance companies, a trader suggested that the new paper will have to compete with older issues sold by Hawaii.
"A lot of insurance companies are full of it, so it has to be relatively attractively priced."
Bid-wanted lists were being circulated, but traders said the volumes appeared fairly light, as the morning activity began. Trading was subdued, however.
In the secondary market, Denver Colorado City and County Airport Revenues of November 2025, which pay a 5.7 percent coupon, were offered at 5.87 percent, NET, up four basis points.
And Florida Ports Financing Commission Revenues of June 2027, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were offered at 5.85 percent, NET, up one basis point.
Municipal bond sales were expected to total $1.1 billion in 30 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
On the competitive side, 11 sales totaling $164 million are on the schedule, a $45 million Oakland, Calif., deal at 1300 EST was the largest.
In the futures markets, the June municipal bond futures fell eight ticks to 112-25/32, while the June Treasury bonds slipped 10 ticks to 108-13/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 140 ticks.
